newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn, soy and wheat steady.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn, soy and wheat steady.

text.p: U.S. FOB Gulf corn, soybean and wheat offers remained steady on Monday as the market focused on the U.S. Department of Agriculture grain stocks report and planting intentions outlook, dealers said.
Export activity was subdued, they said.

USDA on Monday surprised market watchers by releasing a U.S. soybean planting outlook for 1997 of 68.8 million acres. The figure was well above 64.21 million acres planted to soybeans in 1996 and also exceeded an average of analysts' expectations of 65.85 million acres.
USDA said March 1 U.S. corn stocks totaled 4.494 billion bushels, above trade expectations for 4.565 billion.
In export news, two Philippine mills bought 100,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat at about $185 per tonne. The commodity will be shipped between May and July this year, one trader said.
Also, the U.S. Coast Guard said travel restrictions on the Mississippi for some commercial vessels had been further tightened as conditions on the river remain hazardous.

On Friday, the Coast Guard ruled that tank vessels or tank ships with 1,600 gross tons or more carrying certain petroleum products or chemicals, as well as deep-draft chemical tank ships, must travel in daylight hours only downbound between mile 233 (Baton Rouge) and mile 88 (New Orleans) of the river.
